source.title: Training Dynamics of Deep Network Linear Regions
source.authors: Ahmed Imtiaz Humayun; Randall Balestriero; R. Baraniuk

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. Figures are represented by captions and textual descriptions; plotted numerical values are not available in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports grokking-like delayed generalization on MNIST, a non-algorithmic image task, using a weight-scaled initialization regime; this is an extension to a new setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports an MNIST grokking experiment with weights scaled by 8 at initialization and textual descriptions of accuracy timing. It also reports a training-set-size sweep on MNIST. LC-only outcomes, including the weight-decay sweep and random-label memorization results, do not establish the accuracy or circuit claims in the versions. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study induces grokking on MNIST, a non-algorithmic image task, by scaling initial weights by 8 (following Omnigrok). It reports that generalization is delayed relative to memorization. This bears on V3 in a new, non-original setting, though it largely replicates Liu et al. (2022). Its local-complexity (LC) statistic is a geometric partition measure, not a circuit or mechanism measure.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that LC follows a decrease–ascent–descent pattern and that partition regions migrate toward the decision boundary late in training. In induced-grokking MNIST runs, they tie the LC ascent to memorization and the second descent to generalization, and report a second ascent right before grokking. They also report that depth raises the ascent peak and delays generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The grokking experiment uses MNIST and scales weights by 8 at initialization, following Liu et al. (2022); it is not the small modular-arithmetic setup described in the original grokking source.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported timing of generalization changes with network depth: deeper networks generalize later. The paper also reports local-complexity changes under varying data size and regularization, but those do not establish the claim versions' accuracy or circuit outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: In induced-grokking MNIST runs, local complexity around training points shows a second ascent just before delayed generalization begins. Memorization coincides with the first LC ascent, and generalization with the second LC descent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The input-space partition density (local complexity) shows a distinct phase change shortly before grokking, tracking memorization and generalization phases.

fits_no_version.finding: On ground-truth MNIST (default init), more training samples yield earlier and greater generalization and remove the LC ascent peak.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In non-grokking MNIST training, larger datasets advance generalization and suppress the LC ascent associated with memorization.

record.problems: The supplied text gives qualitative descriptions rather than numerical accuracy values or exact depth and dataset-size settings for the relevant figures. The induced-grokking result uses one non-algorithmic dataset and does not report an unscaled-initialization comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant accuracy or progress-measure outcomes were omitted. LC-only results in Figures 7 and 11, including weight-decay and random-label effects, were not entered because they do not measure the accuracy, circuit, or artifact outcomes in the tested versions.

untested.parts: Text or molecule data. Weight norm as a control. An explicit lazy-to-rich analysis. A direct side-by-side of scaled and unscaled initialization in the same figure.
Not tested: there is no algorithmic dataset.
Not tested: no circuit identification, no measure of memorization-component removal.
Not tested. The weight-decay sweep is LC-only, on CIFAR10 CNNs, and does not involve grokking.

missing.what: Unscaled-initialization MNIST MLP runs (depths 2–5, width 200): train and test accuracy peak together during the first LC descent, with no delayed generalization. This is a contrast condition for the ×8-scaled grokking runs.

record.verdict_notes: Removed the reader's V3 limits_scope label: depth changing the delay's length does not qualify the claim that the delay appears. Removed the V2 support label because LC does not measure the circuit mechanism V2 names. The grokking result follows Omnigrok (Liu et al. 2022), which is not an original source here, so this is mainly a replication in a slightly different setup.

versions.untested_parts: No test on a small algorithmic dataset such as modular arithmetic; no reported test of whether smaller algorithmic training sets require more optimization.
Measures local complexity around grokking, but does not identify a Fourier or other generalizing circuit, or show memorizing components being removed.

Tests MNIST with weights scaled by 8 at initialization. Does not compare against an unscaled initialization to demonstrate switching grokking off, test weight norm or a lazy-to-rich transition, or test text or molecule data.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
Does not test whether weight decay selects an efficient generalizing circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifacts.

rows.subject: Fully connected DN (MNIST; varying depth, aggregate as described in text)
rows.operation_detail: Induced grokking by scaling weights at initialization by 8
rows.measure: Timing of generalization on test accuracy relative to training
rows.value: The text says grokking is induced; generalization starts earlier in shallow networks than in deeper networks, and increasing depth delays generalization.
rows.note: The result is described across varying depths; the supplied text does not give exact depth values or numerical accuracy curves.
rows.check: The values are qualitative only: no accuracy numbers, step counts or exact depths for Fig. 8–9 are given. The depth dependence modulates the length of the delay; it does not qualify whether the delay appears.

rows.subject: Fully connected DN (MNIST; varying depth, aggregate as described in text)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked local complexity during training in the induced-grokking setup
rows.measure: Timing of local-complexity changes relative to generalization
rows.value: The text reports a second ascent in local complexity right before the model starts grokking.
rows.uncertainty: 25% of the standard deviation of local complexity is used for confidence intervals in the reported experiments; no uncertainty is stated for this timing result.
rows.note: This is a local-complexity progress measure, not an identification of a circuit or a demonstration that memorizing components are removed.
rows.check: LC is a linear-region density statistic. It does not identify a generalizing circuit or the removal of memorizing components. The 'second ascent right before grokking' is a qualitative timing remark, not a demonstrated continuous progress measure for V2's mechanism. Move to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Depth 3 width 200 MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained with varying numbers of MNIST samples with ground-truth labels
rows.measure: Generalization and its timing as training-set size changes
rows.value: The text says increasing the number of samples increases generalization and makes it occur earlier; the local-complexity ascent phase gradually disappears.
rows.note: This is an MNIST dataset-size sweep, not a test on small algorithmic datasets or a reported grokking-induced initialization condition.
rows.check: This is a dataset-size sweep in the default (non-grokking) MNIST setup. It does not test V1's algorithmic delay versus data size. The 'observed' state is not meaningful for any version.

relationships.condition: MNIST MLPs (MSE loss, 1K samples) with initial weights scaled by 8, across tested depths
relationships.reason: The text reports induced grokking on MNIST: memorization occurs first and generalization is delayed, later still in deeper nets (R1). Unscaled runs in Sec. 4.2 show train and test accuracy peaking together, which points to init scale switching the delay on (from the text, see missing).
relationships.display_finding: Scaling initial weights by 8 induced memorization before generalization, with longer delays in deeper networks, whereas unscaled training and test accuracy peaked together.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
